postTitle: Tax-Loss Harvesting and Asset Location Explained
topic: The same yearly payment keeps more invested in an account without yearly tax

assumptions.notes: Reel's own small example, illustrative: a €100 yearly payment taxed at 25% leaves €75 invested; in an account without yearly tax on the payment, €100. The lesson's household example (about €540 less yearly tax on €400,000) is in the caption.

caption.instagram:
Your investment pays €100 this year. How much stays invested?

It depends on the account. Where that payment is taxed every year, an example tax of one quarter takes €25 and leaves €75 invested. In an account without yearly tax on the payment, such as a pension in many countries, the whole €100 stays invested. Money taken out of such an account may be taxed later.

This is why investments that pay out a lot every year (interest, for example) are commonly held in the accounts without yearly tax, and investments that pay out little in ordinary ones, with the overall mix unchanged. In the lesson's example of a household with €400,000, that placement means about €540 less tax a year.
